(6) PUBLIC HEARING:
6A. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2018-008(SP-2018-008) & PAD AT 113-
133 PLYMOUYH STREET. A public hearing to consider an application
by James Ward for Special Use Permit No. 2018-008 (SP-2018-008)
for a Preliminary Planned Assembly Development (PAD) to allow a
20-unit residential townhome subdivision on a 29,593 square-foot
R-3 (Limited-family Residential) zoned property at 113-133
Plymouth Street.

Mr. Bernard McCrumby made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked for the applicant to come forward and
address the planning commission.

Commissioner Rice asked
   Regarding the mailed notifications to the public and the
  fact that no one from the public was in attendance to speak
  on the project?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that is correct.
   Next he asked about the difference between the spirit of
  the law and the letter or intent of the law, because he
  stated that there were a lot of drastic deviations from the
  code for the PAD on this project is that correct?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated for the PAD that is correct.

Commissioner Rice stated that since the surrounding community
members are not here to object or challenge this project, he
will stand down and let the project go forward.

Commissioner Trejo asked about if
   There will be security fencing that will be at the project
  site?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated yes, there will be security perimeter
  fencing on the east, west and north areas of the subject
  site. Also there will be a fenced wall next to the larger
  area which will be guest parking, adjacent to an alley.
  At present, there has been no mention of the type of
  material that will be used for the fencing by the
  applicant.
   There will be secure access to all of the units on the site
  and in looking at the layout of the plans the large area
  that is on the west side,
  - Mr. McCrumby stated the larger area is actually is the
  pool deck area.
   How is that area accessed if fenced off by both the
  residence and security, will there be a security key given
  to the residents to use for access.
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that access to the pool area for all
  of the residents is a bridge walkway from Plymouth that
  connects both sides of the units to the pool area.
  Perimeter access and walkways to the front of the units
  to pools. There will be subterranean parking that is
  proposed by the applicant for access to all of the units’
  garages. Above that will be a walkway.
  - There will also be a children’s play area that will sit
  above the guest parking area.
  - Ms. Wilcox asked Mr. McCrumby to show the floor plan from
  the street level.

  2
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
October 3, 2018
    For entrance to the property through the driveway, is there
  a security feature that the residents will have to use such
  as a security key? Such as a gate with a security feature?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that at present there is no private
  gate that opens, however there will be a security office
  that will be located at the base of the subterranean
  garage where the security would have access to see who
  will be coming and going and with the help of the 13
  security cameras around the entire property.
    Mail drop offs – will they be dropped off in a central area
  or will the mail be dropped off at each individual units?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that at present there is nothing that
  speaks to a central location for mail drop offs, but that
  is an operations answer that the applicant can speak to.

Commissioner Coleman asked about
   There being any considerations for any handicap residents
  and what are they in regards to upstairs entrances, parking
  and any guests/visitors with needed wheelchair access?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that when the applicant moves onto
  the building and safety component there will be ADA
  requirements that will have to be complied with in order
  to move forward with the projects that will include
  garage parking for handicap van accessibility with
  regards to 8’foot height requirements, elements to assist
  with entrance to the first and second levels. This will
  all be handled in the site plan review.
   Actual security guards on the premises?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated although the number of security
  guards was not mentioned there will be a 24 hour security
  guard on site with security camera monitoring in real
  time.
   The pricing and if there will be any provisions for low-
  income / first-time home buyers?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that the applicant will have to speak
  with regards to the price-points of the project, but
  believes that this project is not an affordable/income
  restricted residential development.

Commissioner Rice asked about
   The original project being 29,593 square-feet, and then
  there is discussion about the reduction of the project due
  to the widening of the street by five-feet by the City, but
  that the project will continue regardless, yet requesting
  new setback.
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that the actual building will be
  pushed back to meet the dedication requirement of five
  feet, and the structure itself being pushed back, on both
  the front and rear of the property, there is up on the
  second level of the main level a reduction in the
  building separation which would help the development to
  meet and still maintain their floor area.

Commissioner Rice asked if the deviation of the front yard, rear
yard and side yard remain the same?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that is correct.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to come forward and address
the Planning Commissioners and speak on their project.

Members of the WARD Shore Developers (James Ward, Sr., James
Ward Jr., Joshua Thompson, Arundel Lanton, Walter Richards,
Nicole Smith, Jack Bryant, Mr. Nassef Eskander, Moheb Gorgy and
Mitchell Morrison of Envicom Corporation answering the questions
  3
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
October 3, 2018
on behalf the Air Quality Analysis, came forward to address the
Planning Commission.

Commissioner Rice asked about
   The CC and R’s and common areas, will they be intact for
  this particular project?
  - Ms. Nicole Smith stated that this particular project does
  not have the regulatory CC and R’s with regards to
  building colors and such, this project gives the single
  family home owner the opportunity to regulate their
  property as they see fit. But, with regards to the
  maintenance areas there is a maintenance agreement with
  the entire project that will be in the form of an HOA
  payment that will be kept.
   Was and How was the neighborhood and all of the residents
  within 500 feet notified about this new project coming on
  board and what was their response?
  - Mr. James Ward Sr., stated there was a door to door
  information notices distributed to over 1,000 of the
  local residents as well as a mail-out, inviting them to
  an info meet and greet at Rodgers Park.

Commissioner Trejo asked about
   How was the response and how many attended?
  - Mr. Ward, Sr., stated that about 40 families attended and
  spoke up mainly concerning the tax revenue of the
  project.
  - Ms. Smith stated that several contractors and journeymen
  who were asking about potential job openings for this
  project, along with possible future job builds.
   Of the attendees who showed for the presentation, do you
  know if they were actual families who live in the area or
  people looking to move into the area?
  - Mr. Ward, Sr., stated that for the most part, they were
  local residents who already live in the area and were
  interested in the project.

Commissioner Coleman asked about
   Will your development be in control of the HOA or the
  residents and will your development keep a hands on
  approach to make sure the residents will do as they are
  required?
  - Mr. Ward, Sr., stated that they will give the residents
  the guidelines that they must follow to ensure that they
  follow what is expected and will make sure that there
  will be a president of the HOA installed as the go-to
  person.
   Security at the property, 13 cameras is not enough, also
  the protection around the pool area is in question, will
  your development company be willing to work with staff
  during the site plan review process?
  - Mr. Ward, Sr., stated that the actual amount of cameras
  will most likely increase by three-times (3x’s) due to
  the types of security coverages that will be placed at
  each residence.
   With regards to having a live security guard on site and
  the real camera time watch, will your development company
  increase the number from one live security guard to at
  least two?
  - Mr. Ward, Sr., stated that actually, the way of the
  future is for each of the residences to have security
  cameras both within their own homes and on their personal
  smart phones/smart systems where each resident will be
  notified in real time and all can see and work together
  4

  in securing their own properties. Having to pay for a
  live person on the premises will be a large increase for
  the property owners to have deal with, we feel the way to
  go is with the latest and newest technology available,
  and least expensive for the residents.

Chairman Springs asked several questions of the developers:
   Why do you want the City to change its regulations and
  guidelines (aka the City Code), to require less from you
  and  relinquish  the  City’s  standards  for  your  new
  development?
  - Ms. Wilcox clarified with regards to what the applicant
  can do and build at the location, also that they did not
  have to come before the planning commission as they are
  mainly working with condominiums. She also stated that
  the applicant is proposing the small lot sub-division,
  where they will divide the land. She stated that she just
  wanted to make the clarification for the commission that
  this project could have taken place as an apartment
  building, but the applicant has chosen condominiums.
  - Ms. Smith stated that it is a multi-family zone, so
  typically it would be developed with apartments and then
  the configuration of those allow a number of the
  properties to use the land, with the small lot
  acquisition, it is home ownership, but it is on land that
  deemed appropriate for multi-family use and the density
  proposed would be allowed by right.
  - Mr. Ward Sr., stated that in addition, the City of Los
  Angeles also has a small lot density usage that is
  starting to be utilized all over the country, due to the
  need for more housing.

    Also about the lot sizes and how if there was a reduction
  in the end-units, how there can be added space? What about
  the open roof-tops and balcony’s that will be for each
  unit? Is there no space for yards?
  - Mr. Ward Sr., stated yes, every unit will have a balcony.
  With regards to added ground space, there will be a small
  front yard and a small back landscaping area.

    With regards to the various sizes of the units and why? How
  many end units will you have for purchase or is it only the
  one this large?
  - Mr. Ward Sr., stated that the architect will speak to the
  various sizes of the units. Mr. Nassef Eskander, stated
  that the different sizes were due to the positioning of
  the units on the lot, thus the end lots were larger in
  size than the interior units.

    Now what are the costs of these units and how are you
  basing the price? Is it by square footage and the larger
  size will be much more?
  - Mr. Ward Sr., stated that the costs begin around $749k
  plus it is not solely based upon the size but with the
  inclusion of a lot of common area along with the lot size
  itself.
  - Ms. Smith stated that the price will be set at current
  market rate, due to the inclusion of the size of the
  home, and the size of the lot and it is a matter of the
  lot itself and also the easement. With the larger unit,
  the easement will also be larger and thus will make it
  difficult at this time to give a conclusive cost.

  5
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
October 3, 2018
    With regards to the community reach-out, how was the
  reaction of the community? What was the reaction to the
  pricing starting at $750k? Who are the people who will be
  able to afford these homes? Are you pricing the people out
  of this neighborhood, or did you have a favorable outcome?
  - Mr. Ward Sr., stated that prior to having the event they
  went throughout the various areas and the pricing was
  very comparable to what they are asking for now.
  - Ms. Smith stated that there was one gentleman in
  particular who spoke and said there were several
  homeowners that are in Inglewood and that their homes
  have appreciated in value and they are looking at homes
  that are upwards towards the same value, so this is a
  great opportunity for those homeowners to be able to stay
  in  the  neighborhood,  yet  down-size  with  less
  responsibility for a lot, but still maintain the quality
  of life that these small lot homes allow.

    He then asked about previous ownership in the city of
  Inglewood by the applicant and they stated that they have a
  property here in the City of Inglewood, Chairman inquired
  where?
  - A property on 3rd Avenue near Arbor Vitae in 2015, for
  $350k, and sold it to a couple who still live in it to
  this day, and it has just been refinanced in upwards of
  over $700k.

    Background checks conducted by the development company? Who
  will monitor the residents before and after their purchase
  of the property to move into this great City of Inglewood?

Commissioner Trejo asked;
   What about the small lot developments by various cities –
  other than Inglewood, and is this something that Inglewood
  has started looking at doing – like the applicant has
  mentioned it as the wave of the future?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated no, not at this time. Los Angeles over
  the past few years has started to adopt the small lot
  standards. Not necessarily because of no interest in
  Inglewood, just that there have been other priorities for
  the City.
   At present the applicant is using the planned assembly
  development in order to accomplish what they call small lot
  development, is that what the City is doing?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated yes, that is correct.

Chairman Springs asked;
   Would this be under the General Plan for the City of
  Inglewood?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that the small lot ordinance would be
  under the Zoning code in the General Plan.

Commissioner Trejo stated;
   The reason she is acknowledging this is that here in
  Inglewood and the South Bay area it is not quite as dense
  as Los Angeles, Burbank and Glendale and some of the other
  cities, where the need for housing is greater.
  - Ms. Wilcox stated it might be important to mention that
  in regards to this property additional units will be
  allowed under the current zone.

Chairman Springs stated that he will close out the questions for
the applicant, and he stated that the location of this new build

Chairman Springs opened up the floor for public comments and
asked the public to line up and speak to the planning commission

FOR: / AGAINST:

Mr. Todd Corey – Inglewood Resident
  - When will this project start, what is the timeline
  - Noise issues
  - Air Quality during the building process

Commissioner Holly answered Mr. Corey’s questions with the
statement that the applicant has in mind the timeline and any

Mr. Mitchell Morrison of ENVICOM, Corporation came forward to
speak on the SCAQD (South Coast Air Quality District) and

7B. DESIGN REVIEW NO. 2018-003 (DR-2018-003) 3330 WEST
MANCHESTER BOULEVARD. A non-public hearing to consider an
application by Caprice L. Collins for Design Review No. 2018-
003 (DR-2018-003) to  allow an LED electronic sign affixed to
the tower element of an existing building in the Art Deco
Overlay zone at 3330 W. Manchester Boulevard.

Ms.  Marissa  Fewell,  Assistant  Planner,  made  the  staff
presentation.

Chairman  Springs  asked  for  questions  from  the  planning
commission to staff.

Commissioner Holly asked what is the difference between this
particular sign being an LED and a regular billboard? Is it like
the new WOW Media signs that are presently flashing images and
videos onto the screen, or is it just lit electronic letters
floating across the sign?

Ms. Fewell stated that any electronic sign can be installed, but
that an LED sign must go through the sign adjustment process,
and this sign has been conditioned to only include text to
advertise for the on-site Law Firm of the applicant – Collins
Law Group, and no images or other advertising on the sign will
be allowed.

Commissioner Rice asked about
   Text only, meaning no graphics at all and
  - Ms. Fewell stated yes, text only the Law Firm business
  logo, but no images.
   How will the words change on the screen, will they flash on
  and off, or float and dance across the screen?
  - Ms. Fewell stated that the LED Company representative
  will be able to answer that question.
   How does it work from advertisement to advertisement?
  - Ms. Fewell stated that the advertisement will only be for
  the on-site law firm and nothing or no one else.
   Was there notice of this sent to the public for their
  notification?
  - Ms. Fewell stated that this is a Design Review and not a
  public hearing so no, the public was not notified of this
  request. If the applicant had applied through the sign
  adjustment process, then the neighboring properties would
  have been notified.

  9
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
October 3, 2018
    Sign Adjustment meaning the size of the sign be reduced to
  9-feet by 2-feet, although the applicant is requesting it
  be enlarged to 10-feet by 4-feet?
  - Ms. Fewell stated yes, the reduced sign area is one of
  the conditions of approval for the LED Sign in the Art
  Deco area.
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that the sign adjustment is required
  because it is an electronic sign, not for the difference
  in size, just because it is an electronic sign. The
  applicant is coming through the Planning Commission
  because Design Review is required due to the Art Deco
  Overlay and because it is an electronic sign, and not
  allowed by right even if it was 9-feet by 2-feet.
